questions.prompt: Five readings of a pressure gauge, in bar: 12.5, 13.1, 12.8, 13.4, 12.7. What is the mean reading? Give it to two decimals.
A sample of five daily counts of rejected castings: 6, 9, 7, 12, 11. What is the sample standard deviation s? Give it to two decimals.
questions.explanation: x̄ = 45 / 5 = 9. The deviations are −3, 0, −2, 3, 2; their squares add to 9 + 0 + 4 + 9 + 4 = 26. s² = 26 / (5 − 1) = 6.5, and s = √6.5 = 2.55 castings. Dividing by n would give √5.2 = 2.28, the population form.

questions.prompt: A call center logs the number of calls that arrive in each 5-minute interval. Calls arrive at random, at an average of 4 per interval. Which distribution models the number of calls in an interval?
options: Poisson
Binomial
Normal
Uniform
questions.explanation: Random events counted in a fixed interval at a mean rate (λ = 4), with no fixed number of trials: Poisson.

questions.prompt: An inspector tests 40 circuit boards from a line where each board, independently, has a 1.5 % chance of a solder fault. Which distribution models the number of faulty boards among the 40?
options: Binomial with n = 40 and p = 0.015
Poisson with λ = 1.5
Normal with μ = 40
Binomial with n = 1.5 and p = 0.40
questions.explanation: A fixed number of independent trials (40 boards), each faulty with the same probability 0.015: binomial with n = 40 and p = 0.015.

questions.prompt: A 95 % confidence interval for the mean thickness of a coating is 48.6 to 51.2 µm. The specification asks for a mean thickness between 45 and 55 µm. What is the best conclusion?
options: The process mean meets the specification: the whole interval is inside 45 to 55 µm
95 % of coatings are between 48.6 and 51.2 µm
The process fails, because the interval is not centered on 50 µm
Nothing can be concluded without the p-value
questions.explanation: Every plausible value of the mean lies inside the specification for the mean. The interval is about the mean, not about 95 % of individual coatings.

questions.prompt: A test of whether a new heat treatment changes the mean hardness gives p = 0.012. The engineer set α = 0.05. What is the conclusion?
options: Reject H₀: the data show that the mean hardness changed
Do not reject H₀: there is no change
The heat treatment is proven to be better
The result is not significant, because p is not below 0.01
questions.explanation: p = 0.012 is below α = 0.05, so H₀ (no change) is rejected. The test shows a change, not that it is "better" or that the change is large enough to matter: look at the size of the difference too.

questions.prompt: For a sample of tube wall thicknesses, Q1 = 14.2 mm and Q3 = 15.8 mm. What is the upper fence, Q3 + 1.5 × IQR, beyond which a value is an outlier? Give it to one decimal.

The histogram of 200 pump repair times has a tall peak at 1 to 2 hours and a long tail out to 12 hours. The mean is 2.9 h and the median 1.8 h. How is the distribution shaped, and which number best describes a typical repair?
options: Positively (right) skewed; the median, 1.8 h
Negatively (left) skewed; the mean, 2.9 h
Symmetric; the mean, 2.9 h
Positively skewed; the mean, 2.9 h
questions.explanation: A long tail of large values, with the mean pulled above the median, is positive skew. The few long repairs pull the mean up, so the median is the better description of a typical repair.

questions.prompt: Filled bottles on a stable line vary by a few milliliters from one to the next. After a new batch of bottles arrives, one bottle in twenty is badly underfilled. Which is the better description?
options: The small bottle-to-bottle spread is common-cause variation; the underfills after the new batch point to a special cause
Both are common-cause variation: one bottle in twenty is part of the normal spread, so nothing should be done
Both are special causes: any bottle that is not exactly on target points to something to be found and removed
Neither is variation that matters, because the average fill of the line stays the same after the new batch
questions.explanation: A steady small spread present all the time is common-cause variation, part of the process. A change that starts with a specific event (a new batch of bottles) is a special cause, to be found and removed.

questions.prompt: Two lathes turn shafts with a tolerance of 20.00 ± 0.06 mm. Both are centered on 20.00 mm. Lathe A's standard deviation is 0.01 mm and lathe B's 0.03 mm. What does this mean for quality?
options: Lathe B makes more shafts out of tolerance: its ±3s spread (±0.09 mm) is wider than the tolerance, while A's (±0.03 mm) fits well inside it
Both make the same share of good shafts: both are centered on 20.00 mm, and the centering decides conformance
Lathe A makes more shafts out of tolerance: its smaller spread (±0.03 mm) leaves it less room to stay inside the limits
Neither makes any shaft out of tolerance: both are centered, so their shafts average 20.00 mm, inside 20.00 ± 0.06 mm
questions.explanation: Conformance is decided shaft by shaft, so the spread matters. Nearly all of a process lies within ±3s: ±0.03 mm for A fits inside ±0.06 mm; ±0.09 mm for B does not, so B makes shafts outside the tolerance.
